diagnosis:
Three checks fail consistently across all settled rollouts (C4, C5, C6), while C1/C2/C3/P1 pass reliably. The decisive facts PF1 and PF2 are always revealed and always cited in justification_fact_ids, so the failure is not disclosure or provenance. The problem is ENCODING MISMATCH on all three failing checks: the settlements encode the same correct information in natural phrasings that the checks' exact-string or field-name expectations do not match.

C4 (PF2, 0/4): ENCODING MISMATCH. PF2 is revealed in every rollout and cited in justification_fact_ids in every settled rollout. The settlements correctly defer V-14 and correctly tie its work to the 1600 shipment arrival. Rollout 0: deferred_vehicle_work_date = "tomorrow at 1600". Rollout 1: "tomorrow after 1600". Rollout 3: "after 1600 tomorrow, following completion of V-19". All three are natural encodings of "work begins when the 1600 shipment arrives," but C4 fails in every case — it apparently expects a verbatim string the model never produces (likely "1600 tomorrow" or "tomorrow at 1600" exactly). The model is using the information correctly; the check is too narrow.

C5 (PF1, 0/4): ENCODING MISMATCH. PF1 is revealed in every rollout and cited in justification_fact_ids in every settled rollout. The settlements correctly make V-11 first priority and include the 0600-1000 tasking. Rollout 0 encodes it in the commitment detail: "V-11 is first priority: tire replacement begins at 0700 tomorrow and completes by 1100." Rollout 1 encodes it in a commitment: "Must be complete before 0600 tasking the day after tomorrow." Rollout 3 encodes it in a commitment: "Post the signed V-11 tasking from the operations cell to the maintenance board." C5 fails in all three — it is looking for a specific field name or exact string (likely a "maintenance_board_update" commitment type or a verbatim phrase) that the model does not produce consistently. The information is present and correctly applied; the check wording does not match natural model output.

C6 (PF2, 0/4): ENCODING MISMATCH. PF2 is revealed in every rollout and cited in justification_fact_ids in every settled rollout. The settlements correctly include a supply-tracker update commitment. Rollout 0: commitment type "maintenance_priority_order" with detail mentioning V-14's shipment. Rollout 1: commitment type "supply_update" with target "Battalion supply tracker" and detail "Ensure V-14's dedicated tire shipment (arriving by 1600 tomorrow) is reflected in the battalion supply tracker." Rollout 3: commitment type "supply_tracker_update" with target "Lt. Farouk" and detail "Update the battalion supply tracker with the confirmed V-14 tire delivery by 1600 tomorrow." C6 fails in all three — it apparently expects an exact commitment type string (likely "supply_tracker_update") or a specific target field value, but the model uses three different natural encodings ("maintenance_priority_order"/"supply_update"/"supply_tracker_update"). The information is present and correctly applied; the check is too narrow.

Rollout 2 auto-failed on turn cap (turn_count 10, settled=false). This is a STRUCTURAL problem, not a pacing problem. Both decisive facts were revealed by turn 5, and by turn 8 A1 had already synthesized a complete, correct plan and asked for confirmation. A2's turn 6 produced an unparsable model output (malformed JSON), which appears to have disrupted the settle-eligibility flow. The conversation continued with A3 and A1 both confirming the plan (turns 7-9) but A1 never issued a settle action. Raising turn_cap alone would not reliably fix this because the settle-eligibility condition apparently requires something the malformed turn disrupted. The fix is to loosen the settle-eligibility condition so that a single unparsable turn does not block settlement when all facts have been revealed and the decision-maker has synthesized the plan.
